candidate_relations.reason: A temporally linked vaccine exposure frames an allergic reaction, which conflicts with the spontaneous (non-allergic) CSU definition.
Pruritus and urticaria 7 hours after vaccination are an allergic reaction to vaccination, not chronic spontaneous disease.
Vaccine-induced anaphylaxis requires rapid-onset systemic involvement; this patient had visible urticaria without airway compromise at 7 hours.
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome is listed, but there are no mast-cell mediator levels or chronic activation features to support EDS-associated MCAD.
Lower-lip angioedema without airway compromise is a manifestation of the acute hive episode, not CSU as a chronic diagnosis.
Allergy to a vaccine component is a hypothesized trigger and conflicts with labeling the episode chronic spontaneous urticaria.
Normal CBC, ESR, CRP, and C4 do not establish a mast-cell activation disorder as the CSU equivalent.
Mast-cell activation syndrome requires recurrent mediator symptoms; this is a single post-vaccination urticarial episode with normal inflammatory labs.
Mastocytosis is not supported by a normal complete blood count or by any cutaneous mastocytosis lesions.
Visible knee and popliteal hives after vaccination are allergic urticaria, a conflicting mechanism from spontaneous CSU.
Ehlers–Danlos-associated urticaria is not a standard entity here; EDS is comorbidity and the hives followed vaccination.
The photographs document urticaria, the parent lesion, without the chronic (≥6 week) spontaneous specifier required by CSU.
Idiopathic urticaria is the older near-synonym of CSU but still omits documented chronicity in this 7-hour post-vaccine presentation.

case_quality_flags: Onset 7 hours after first vaccination without a ≥6-week course does not meet Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria; the record supports acute post-vaccine urticaria instead.
